page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-48 is an arm64-based server instance powered by 48 dedicated physical cores of the Neoverse-V2 processor architecture. It features 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1D cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 80 MB of L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography support. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities and memory performance. The instance achieved a top-tier rating in PassMark memory score and database operations, alongside strong read and write memory bandwidth. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput also reached top-tier levels. Single-core performance, measured via stress-ng and PassMark CPU tests, falls into the average range, though multi-core stress-ng performance remains strong.

From a resource density perspective, the c4a-highmem-48 offers high memory capacity per core, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The primary tradeoff is the reliance on the arm64 architecture, which requires compatible software binaries, and the average single-core CPU performance compared to some x86 alternatives.

This server configuration is highly suited for memory-intensive applications, including large-scale database operations, Redis caching layers, static web serving at scale, and multi-threaded data decompression tasks. It is also capable of handling moderate LLM inference workloads, particularly for text generation using medium-sized models.
